statements.text: you choose the primary region when the environment is created, for example the US, Canada, the UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Japan, Singapore or Australia, as capacity and your entitlements allow. It cannot be changed afterwards.
pages are delivered through Adobe's integrated CDN, and up to three additional publish regions can be licensed.
content being worked on is held in the US and published content is distributed globally. For a specific jurisdiction, or tenancy that cannot be shared, Adobe offers a single sovereign setup.
delivery runs on two fully redundant edge providers, through Adobe's managed CDN or your own (Akamai, Cloudflare, Fastly or Amazon CloudFront). It is operated outside China.
on Adobe Experience Platform, which runs on Microsoft Azure or Amazon Web Services, with hosting locations including the US, Canada, the UK, the Netherlands, India and Australia.

you choose the region when Adobe provisions the platform, in North America, Europe or Asia Pacific, and Customer Journey Analytics keeps its data in that same region. Data cannot be moved to another data center later.

runs on central clusters in Oregon, Dublin and Singapore and edge clusters in the Americas, Europe and Asia Pacific, and keeps each visitor's profile on the edge cluster closest to them. Target has no edge cluster in China.

stored on AWS in a single region, with no replication to another region, and copied six ways across three availability zones within that region. Its data centers are in Ashburn, San Jose, Sydney, London and Amsterdam.
each customer is hosted on a Workfront cluster in its US or EU region.

runs on AWS and Azure and is available globally, with production environments in a given region confirmed by Adobe. Commerce on cloud infrastructure is not offered in China or Russia, and its backups stay in the same region as production.
keeps no personal data or private content, and raw CDN logs are not kept after processing; only derived or aggregated data is kept.
Adobe's Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, ISO 9001, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, ISO 22301 and CSA STAR Level 2 for Adobe Experience Cloud, which includes these products.

the list also marks Adobe Experience Cloud GLBA ready, meaning the service can be used in a way that helps you meet your legal obligations for service providers, while you remain responsible for your own compliance.
Adobe's Trust Center lists Commerce on cloud infrastructure with SOC 2 Type 2 (Security + HIPAA) and as a PCI DSS 4.0 compliant service provider.

Commerce as a Cloud Service lists SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001, and the Commerce infrastructure is PCI DSS compliant; you keep PCI compliance for your own custom code and extensions, and cardholder data must not be stored in Commerce.
We will attach Adobe's current certification list for each product in this proposal, from the Adobe Trust Center.
AEM Sites, AEM Publish and Edge Delivery Services are HIPAA-ready with Adobe's Extended Security for Healthcare; the Universal Editor is not.
AEM Assets is HIPAA-ready with Adobe's Extended Security for Healthcare; Content Hub is not.
not HIPAA-ready.
not HIPAA-ready.
Adobe's Healthcare Shield add-on is designed to make Experience Platform applications HIPAA ready.
HIPAA-ready features need the health care add-on for Adobe Commerce, and HIPAA is not available on Commerce as a Cloud Service.
uses TLS 1.2 or greater in transit and AES256 at rest, with keys managed by two independent cloud providers.
data is stored with provider-managed encryption keys by default, and customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault can be turned on for the program in Cloud Manager.

all data is encrypted in transit and at rest, connections use HTTPS with TLS 1.2, and stored data sits in an isolated store unique to your organization. Customer-managed keys come with Adobe's Healthcare Shield or Privacy and Security Shield add-on and cannot be switched back to system-managed keys once set up.
Commerce as a Cloud Service encrypts stored data at rest with AES 256-bit and all data in transit with TLS 1.2 or greater.
every instance is encrypted at rest with AES 256-bit.
connections require TLS 1.2.
browser connections and API integrations require TLS 1.2.
all data is encrypted in transit over HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or greater, and stored data is encrypted at rest with AES 256-bit.

Your team signs in to the Adobe products in this proposal through the Adobe Admin Console. Single sign-on uses Federated IDs with any SAML 2.0 identity provider, such as Okta, Ping Identity or AD FS, or with Microsoft Entra ID over OpenID Connect.
Adobe sign-in covers your authors, administrators and developers, not your site's visitors.
authors sign in through the identity provider behind the site's content source, such as Microsoft or Google, and site authentication can limit preview and publish to authorized requests.
single sign-on is managed in the Admin Console, and where a subscription is on Adobe identity without it, Marketo Support sets it up.
single sign-on is handled through the Adobe Business Platform.

Commerce as a Cloud Service connects to identity providers such as Azure AD and Okta over SAML or OIDC; on Commerce on cloud infrastructure, Adobe sign-in for the Admin is optional and turned on for each instance.
access is controlled with roles and policies that link users with permissions and sandboxes.
access is assigned in the Admin Console, with permissions inherited from your Adobe organization and a full audit trail.
Adobe posts the availability of all its services at status.adobe.com.
a 99.99% service level is a separately licensed option, applied together with an Additional Publish Region on the same program. Sandboxes are not covered by the service level.
has the same service level agreement as AEM as a Cloud Service and runs on multiple CDNs, so delivery can switch to another CDN during an outage. Adobe acknowledges every incident within 15 minutes.

content can be restored from continuous backups within the past 24 hours or from system backups within the past seven days; a restore covers content, not code. In a data-region outage, Adobe restores staging and production from off-site backups.

Adobe lists 99.99% for infrastructure and 99.9% for the application on Commerce on cloud infrastructure, and 99.9% for both on Commerce as a Cloud Service. Pro projects run across three availability zones, each a separate data center, with live backups.
performance is backed by the Adobe Service Level Agreement.
data is copied six ways across three availability zones within its region.
Adobe's Trust Center lists the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) under Adobe-wide privacy.
Adobe Experience Cloud, which includes these products, holds a TrustArc GDPR privacy practices validation and the TrustArc APEC Privacy Recognition for Processors certification.
requests to access and delete personal data go through Adobe's Privacy Service, and integrated products respond within 30 days.

data usage labels on datasets and fields drive governance and access policies, audiences inherit their datasets' labels, and policies are enforced automatically when audiences are activated. Consent from your consent platform flows into profiles, and Experience Platform is a registered IAB TCF 2.0 vendor. Consent policies and their automatic enforcement need Adobe's Healthcare Shield or Privacy and Security Shield.
retention is set separately for the profile store and the data lake.
profiles that opt out are left out of later messages, and every message must let customers unsubscribe. Its system data is kept 90 days in the profile store and 13 months in the data lake.
visitor profiles expire after 14 days of inactivity by default, or up to 90 days if set, and opt-in is supported through tags.
governance settings are inherited from Experience Platform, labels stop or warn users who build metrics from sensitive fields, and consent data can be reported on.
activity history is kept for 25 months, or 37 with the premium data retention option.
keeps no personal data or private content, and raw CDN logs are not kept after processing.

conversation history is available to you for 30 days and then deleted automatically, and it is stored for analytics only with the visitor's consent. Visitors who opt out still get helpful answers, without behavioral personalization.
Adobe's Privacy Service does not delete data inside the Commerce application; access and delete requests there are handled in Commerce.
data protection requests are run by your team, by hand or through APIs, and AEM supports a cookie opt-out service.
the site's operational telemetry uses no cookies or other client-side IDs.
privacy requests are made through a form.
form features on the site need an AEM Forms license; without one, forms are limited to authoring in a spreadsheet.
licensed only together with AEM Sites.

automated consent enforcement and customer-managed keys come with Adobe's Privacy and Security Shield add-on, licensed with each of Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer and Customer Journey Analytics you use.
Experience Platform features beyond Brand Concierge, such as Real-Time CDP, need their own licenses.
needs a license to the Adobe products it works in.
Adobe licenses each product in this proposal and provides its quote; we will include it with this proposal.
Prime or Ultimate, per 1,000 person profiles (B2C) or businessperson profiles (B2B).
Select, Prime or Ultimate, per 1,000 engageable profiles.
Foundation, Select, Prime or Ultimate packages.
Standard or Premium, by annual page views; Premium adds automated personalization, Auto-Target and Recommendations.
licensed by prompts per year, with up to 1,000 optimizations a year across up to 10 LLMs, and includes Semrush Enterprise AIO.
Prime or Ultimate, by content requests per month; Ultimate adds Auto-Optimize.
Commerce as a Cloud Service is licensed per base package, with 1 production and 2 sandbox environments.
per 1,000 conversations a year, which do not roll over, with up to 5 sandboxes.
AI Credits, licensed through the Adobe account team.
Select, Prime or Ultimate, per 1,000 contacts.
Workflow Select, Prime or Ultimate, per user per year.
by content requests per month, with Adobe's CDN included.
licensed for AEM Sites, with up to 1 terabyte of storage.
new customers license Prime or Ultimate; Ultimate includes Adobe Express.

confirm.text: Brand Concierge region: Adobe's FAQ says personal data from a conversation "stays local in line with applicable regional regulations", and Adobe's March 2026 security overview says every part runs in US-East. It stays out of the response until Adobe says which is current.

Brand Concierge and AI training: Adobe's FAQ says it is "specifically trained on your organization's content and customer data", and the March 2026 security overview says "Adobe does not use customer data to train Brand Concierge". It stays out of the response until Adobe says which is current.
Experience Platform regions: Adobe's pages list them differently (India as IND1 or IND2; Switzerland only on the Customer Journey Analytics page). Confirm the region your client needs is offered.

Experience Platform on AWS: Adobe says it is "currently available to a limited number of customers". The response names AWS as an option Adobe offers, not a promise; confirm it with Adobe if your client needs AWS.
Target hosting: Adobe's page says both "Adobe-owned and Adobe-leased data centers" and "hosted on AWS". The response names only the cluster cities.
Marketo data center: Adobe's page still lists some subscriptions as moving to AWS. Confirm your client's data center and pod.

FedRAMP and IRAP on Adobe's Trust Center list cover named offerings only: FedRAMP Tailored applies to Adobe Analytics and Adobe Campaign, FedRAMP Moderate to AEM Gov Cloud and Connect Gov Cloud, and IRAP to Customer Journey Analytics Australia and AEM Gov Cloud Australia at Protected Level. The response leaves them out; name one only if your client is on that offering.
Workfront cluster: Adobe's pages list the EU clusters differently and still describe a move to AWS for some clusters. Confirm your client's cluster.
Commerce App Builder storage: Adobe's Commerce security page says there is no encryption of data kept in App Builder storage. Check whether the build uses it.
Coworker: Adobe's Workfront pages say Coworker is not currently available to organizations in health care, finance or some other industries with sensitive data. Confirm your client is eligible.
